summary: Current main already contains fixes for most originally reported Kimi-K2 parser failures, but still emitted a fragmented <|tool_call_end|> prefix as tool arguments. Hold back only a trailing prefix of that marker until the next increment resolves it. Regression coverage verifies failing-before/passing-after behavior, preservation of a diverging marker-like literal, and two long nested calls with emoji and tiny argument chunks.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before run on the recorded base behavior with tests added but source unmodified: split end-marker text leaked into JSON; the initial one-character-whole-stream stress layout also exposed the existing ambiguity between a literal '<' and a one-character marker prefix. Raw log: reports/j-fc25395b71cf/failing-before.txt. The stress test was then narrowed to tiny argument chunks and explicit multi-character marker splits so it independently tests the evidenced defect without changing the detector's documented literal-'<' behavior.

Focused passing-after regression and two independent boundaries: divergent marker-like payload preservation and >5 KB nested/emoji arguments across two calls. 3 passed. Raw log: reports/j-fc25395b71cf/passing-after-focused.txt.
Complete dedicated Kimi-K2 function/reasoning detector suite: 63 passed and 7 subtests passed. Raw log: reports/j-fc25395b71cf/passing-after-full.txt.
Legacy Kimi-K2 parser compatibility tests: 6 passed. Raw log: reports/j-fc25395b71cf/passing-after-legacy-kimik2.txt.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and correction are deterministic CPU string-stream parsing only; no model forward pass or GPU kernel is involved. No unrelated GPU smoke was used as evidence.

remaining_limitations: Kimi-K2/K2.5 model weights and the reported 8-GPU deployments were unavailable, so full serving/UI behavior, model output quality, and distributed execution were not reproduced.
The regression directly validates parser increments and does not claim a full HTTP serving-path reproduction.

A stream that splits every special marker after a single literal '<' remains indistinguishable from normal text under the detector's existing documented behavior that emits a trailing literal '<'; the added long test uses one-character argument chunks and realistic multi-character marker fragments.
